clue.text: Cool stall selling marine produce?

definitions.meaning: cool in manner means aloof and reserved
a ..., read as a phrase, is a stall selling seafood

explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is cool and distant towards others; the second sense splits the word into a stall of seafood.

clue.text: Dormitory accommodation problem raised in reserves

indicators.note: the reversed problem sits inside the word for reserves

parts.note: subs are substitutes, reserve players

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for problem is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A shortage of student dormitory places has become a problem for the reserve team.
explanation.walkthrough: A dormitory town is one that commuters only sleep in, so 'Dormitory' belongs to the definition, not to a student hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormitory towns are commuter areas where workers merely sleep, the outer residential districts of a city.

clue.text: Scope — a doctor needs it

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

clue.text: Nudist worked on railway business

indicators.note: the letters of the word are worked into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Industry means commerce or manufacturing, a field of business activity.

clue.text: Lobby organisation's initial greeting

clue.text: Spot small cottage around the west of Portugal

clue.text: New arrival anticipating fine instrument

clue.text: Various stores renovated in a day?

clue.text: The bench come to a decision

to resolve or decide a matter

clue.text: Proper sort of pink flower

rose is a pinkish colour

clue.text: Money-grabbing drunk clutching broken cane

parts.note: merry means tipsy, slightly drunk

indicators.note: broken means the letters are shattered and reassembled

clue.text: Flounce downstairs after coat

clue.text: Nick is inside, lying for the most part

parts.note: prone means lying face down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for prison. 'for the most part' cuts PRONE to PRON.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the nick is a jail or police station.

clue.text: Beginning northern climb

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: Starting out on the northern climb.

clue.text: Labour-saving item in the laboratory? Not really!

parts.words: Labour-saving item in the laboratory? Not really!
parts.note: IVF conception happens in lab glassware, not in childbirth labour, so the joke is that it does not truly save labour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' is childbirth: a baby conceived in the lab, as in IVF, still has to be born.
